utterances.text: Thank you. There is an audio recording of this interview, right?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO  STIJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the interview was recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUNNY
utterances.text: Your Honour. I wish to object at this stage. This does not arise out of anything in cross-examination. I did not ask the witness any questions about his interview with OTP. My friend did. My learned friend did ask him in-chief yesterday about this interview and he mentioned an hour and a half. He's now revisiting that interview with no basis from cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic, how does it arise in re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I spent all this time expecting that my learned friend would have an audio recording of this interview, which they had promised. Stijakovic is leaving in a matter of seconds and this recording is something that I wish to tender into evidence, since I don't have a transcript and the transcript should already have been translated into English. I don't have the B/C/S either, because very often there are errors in the English translation. I'm not saying that this sort of thing is done deliberately, but we have the audio recording which is an accurate reflection of Mr. Stijakovic's interview; and on the other hand, we have a poor English translation. If I tender that, it should be easy enough for you, through CLSS, to know what the matter really is. I like that interview. It's very convenient for me. And I wanted to tender it under Rule 68 as video evidence. I can't have the whole thing admitted into evidence. Why didn't I react earlier? Because up to now I had been expecting to receive a B/C/S transcript, which I have not. I did say that I'd be tendering that under Rule 68.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic, at the moment, I don't believe this to be a matter for re-examination. However, the Chamber would give you leave, when you receive the audio recording, to seek to tender it if you think it is in some way material to questions that have arisen. We do that because you had not received it at the time when you led your evidence and re-examined. So that matter can be left on that basis for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUNNY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could interject at this moment to clarify. It's my understanding that the audio recording was indeed delivered prior to Mr. Stijakovic commencing his testimony and an English translation was provided shortly thereafter. There were difficulties in having that typed up in time to be made available with the recording. The recording was made available I think a day or two after the interview took place. The English translation I provided to my learned friend before Mr. Stijakovic gave his evidence and a formal copy was disclosed formally today but he was in receipt of the English translation. And I'm told from my office, Your Honour, that B/C/S transcripts, a full transcript of what is on the tape rather than an English translation is something not normally requested or provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We are told, Mr. Borovic, that you had the audio tape some days before.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I've been very clear. I got the audio. I listened to the audio. And I ascertained that the English translation was indeed a very poor one. What I asked my learned friend to do is to submit to us a transcript in the B/C/S so that we might have it displayed on our monitors so that the witness can go through it and confirm its authenticity or lack thereof. And they say that on account of the Scottish accent, they weren't able to get it translated or something like that. But there is nothing special in that transcript. There is nothing there that isn't in the interview that he provided to the OTP. This is only evidence that a man in the absence of Defence counsel is repeating the same thing word by word. I think that can buttress this witness's credibility if it is ever challenged. I missed my opportunity if indeed I burnt my bridges behind me by not receiving a timely translation, then that's all right, I guess. However, I do think it is the case that the Prosecution were late serving these copies on us. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Lunny.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUNNY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, I would submit that my learned friend is attempting to lodge a statement as an exhibit to show consistency for the point of view of bolstering credibility, and in my submission that is not admissible. One can use prior statements where they are inconsistent to attack credibility but they cannot be used to promote credibility. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lunny. I was misled in my own understanding earlier by thinking that Mr. Borovic had not received the audio tape before the evidence of the witness commenced. At the moment, there is no apparent reason or basis upon which that audio tape or a transcript of it would be admissible in evidence. The witness has been called and given his evidence. There was some cross-examination as to whether certain things were said to the representatives of the Defence in the course of his proofing, but that's not the issue that is dealt with on these tapes. Therefore, unless there is some further issue which hasn't become clear at the present time, Mr. Lunny's objection is well-founded. We, I'm afraid, Mr. Borovic, have come to the point that the witness has given his evidence, he's told us what he says occurred. In so far as it's relevant, which is scantly so, he has told us that he has put certain things to you and certain things to the Prosecution when he's been questioned, but what is relevant, as far as we are concerned, is the evidence that he's given here. And you've been able to cross-examine, having heard the audio tape of his questioning, and I'm sure that if there was something material revealed in that, the matter could properly have been addressed in the course of your questioning. So we must leave that subject matter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I accept your ruling and will not be raising any further points. Next, can this entry from a part of the copied diary be brought up on our monitors? It's 2D 14-0001. Can we have the page bearing the 10th of November brought up?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stijakovic, can you see this?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO  STIJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have it yet. The 10th of November? I don't have that. I have the 3rd of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Could we please have the 10th of November, 1991.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO  STIJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's fine. I can see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Would you please be so kind, sir, although it might be slightly tiring, to tell us exactly what you wrote down on the 10th of November? But, please, the entire entry. I won't be interrupting you like the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO  STIJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Based on a previous plan of attack the battalion carried out an action and took Milovo Brdo, the last important point along the axis of attack of the battalion. The focus of the attack was on the action of the 3rd Assault Group which, having received support, took the sector. The 2nd Assault Group remained blocked and the 1st Assault Group took the sector of the school and the kindergarten. In the course of today's action, nine of our men were wounded and two killed. These men were members of our unit. We shall further be planning our own actions depending on the actions carried out by our neighbours."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Full stop, right? Thank you very much. Mr. Stijakovic, look at the 11th of November, 1991, now. Would you please read out the first sentence. And if there is any need, we can have the entire paragraph read out. But what does the first sentence say?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO  STIJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The 11th November. Today we did not carry out any offensive action. Rather, we rested our men."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Comma?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO  STIJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "We put our combat disposition back together and we organised for the lines reached to be firmly held."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Stijakovic, the next day is the 12th of November; isn't that right? Could you please read aloud the first two sentences in that entry.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO  STIJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The 12th of November. Today the battalion organised the sorting out of the combat disposition. We carried out no actions with the exception of having the 1st Assault Group join up along August Cesarac street."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The 13th of November is the only date that was invoked by my learned friend. You read in that entry that the battalion was carrying out combat actions in a settlement at the foot of Milovo Brdo. My question is: Which settlement is it? Which neighbourhood at the foot of Milovo Brdo? Is that the Milovo Brdo area?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO  STIJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Geographically speaking, this is still the Milovo Brdo area.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can we now go to the 14th of November, 1991, please. Can you please read that bit since it's a short one.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO  STIJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Today the battalion managed to sort out its combat disposition. We did not carry out any actions. Instead we prepared our men for further actions. We organised for a regular flow of supplies and for replenishment in order to continue actions."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Stijakovic, can you now please read the following entry, the 15th of November, 1991.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO  STIJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The 15th of November. Today the battalion prepared for the following action. We did not have any wounded or killed. We prepared our future actions and we were sorting out the combat disposition of our units."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. If it's not too hard, we have the 16th of November before what you previously read. What is your entry say?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO  STIJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The 16th of November. Today the battalion carried out preparations for future actions. We have organised regular supplies for our men. The unit was visited by the brigade commander and while speaking to soldiers, he demanded that further support be lent to the actions of the assault detachment."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Stijakovic, ever since this period of time, the 10th, the 11th, the 12th, the 13th, the 14th, the 15th, and the 16th of November, 1991, did you ever find yourself along any axis of operations or in the midst of an action that would not be consistent with what you wrote down in this entry or did you stay in the Milovo Brdo area throughout?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO  STIJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The units of the 1st Motorised Battalion did not go anywhere else but the Milovo Brdo area at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Next: Mr. Stijakovic, my learned friend quoted for your benefit a portion of the order by Operations Group South dated the 14th of November, 1991, which you had already interpreted for our benefit over the last day, so I would just like to read out a single line to you from item 4. That's the most famous one. And this is what he told you: "Assault Detachment 1 (minus the 1st Motorised Battalion) from their present sector of combat disposition to be transferred to the following axis: Dalmatinska street-Alije Alijagica-water-tower." Isn't that what says?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO  STIJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My learned friend further said -- or, rather, asked you why this small element of Assault Detachment 1, the weaker element, which was his graphic expression, why did they not get any support from Radic's 3rd Company, which had previously turned out to be an exceptionally capable unit. My -- that was the question of the Prosecutor and you answered what you answered. Can you now please read out the assignment for Assault Detachment 1 which is just underneath item 4? I'll read it out for your benefit, since you don't have it on the screen. "Assignment, in close cooperation with the 2nd Battalion of the military police, Assault Detachment 4, take control of buildings in the following area, Alije Alijagica street, Stjepan Supanac school, and get as fast as possible to the Slavija area and the water-tower in order to prevent a withdrawal of the Ustasha forces from the Mitnica area." Full stop. This Assault Detachment 1, on this axis that I've just read out to you, are they alone there or are they actually working closely with the 2nd Battalion of the military police and Assault Detachment 4 as I've just read out?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO  STIJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's just like you've read out. Assault Detachment 1 minus the 1st Motorised Battalion was working closely with the above-mentioned units along this axis of operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. What the Prosecutor failed to read out today is the following item, item 5. Can we please show that to the witness since I'm nearing the ends of my re-examination or perhaps you have that in front of you. Please try to track it down. It's number 4. This is Exhibit 430. Can you please read out item 5 because this is something that you were not confronted with today. My learned friend stated that you had never been taken from Assault Detachment 1. Exhibit 430. I'm sorry, Your Honours. Just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO  STIJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can we just please blow this up slightly?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: We have the B/C/S on our monitors. I'm not sure if the Chamber has that.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO  STIJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The 1st Motorised Battalion from their present sector of combat disposition secure the line reached, establish full control" --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Just a minute. I don't think the Chamber have this on their screens so ... I will repeat this for you. My learned friend has read out to you item 4. He said Assault Detachment 1 was alone but you've read out the assignment now, and it appears they were working with other units. So what I want to look at now is item 5. Read it out, please.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO  STIJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The 1st Motorised Battalion from its present sector of combat disposition secured the line reached, establish full control over the area conquered, and coordinate action with the attacking forces along the following axis: Sundarciceva street and Marsala Tita street. Be at the ready for active action along the following axis: Milovo Brdo and the bridges over the river Vuka."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The question is: The axis of operations of Assault Detachment 1 is Dalmatinska-Alije-Alijagica-water-tower. Is that the axis of operations that you were -- you were on or were you at the opposite end near Sundarciceva street and Marsala Tita street? Are these two different streets leading to the water-tower?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO  STIJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, these are two entirely different streets. The 1st Motorised Battalion was headed for the downtown area and the bridges.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. I asked if these were two entirely different axes of operations.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO  STIJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours could we please have 431, Exhibit 431 brought up on our monitors? This is the OG South order dated the 16th of November, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You read that yesterday. I won't make you go through this again. If we look at the item called the assignments for units, under number 1 it says: "The 1st Motorised Battalion, in keeping with the assignment given on the 14th of November, 1991, and with the support of some elements of the armoured battalion of the Guards Motorised Brigade continue the attack along the axis," so and so. Sundarciceva street and so on and so forth. What does all of this mean again? I'm also asking you this: On the 16th of November, along your own axis, a predesignated axis, Milovo Brdo but also the axis that you would reach at a later stage. But at this point in time Assault Detachment 1 is along a different axis on the 16th of November, 1991.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO  STIJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this order, we are heading for the downtown area and the bridges. However, we carried out this particular assignment simply by firing, for the simple reason that there was no need for us to go further down. Once at Milovo Brdo, you have a great view of all the three bridges.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Assault Detachment 1 was not along the same axis on the 16th of November, 1991. They were elsewhere. Isn't that a fact? Because that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUNNY
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Lunny?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUNNY
utterances.text: I have an objection. My friend is leading on that point. I would prefer if he ask the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think you're right, Mr. Lunny, but to what effect?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Where is Assault Detachment 1 under the command of Borivoje Tesic at this point in time, which axis?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO  STIJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this point in time it's at Milovo Brdo, "vodo toranj," the water-tower.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try to explain something for the benefit of my colleague. I think that he --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note we did not understand Mr. Borovic's remark at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lunny.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUNNY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have a secondary objection with regard to the point put to the witness. There seems to be no reference to 1st Assault Detachment within that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you putting to the witness that the document is dealing with the 1st Assault Detachment, Mr. Borovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm sure you know this, but it's down to the ability of my learned friend to see what the order dated the 14th of November might mean, and then the order dated the 16th of November refers you back to the order date the 14th of November and it's all pretty obvious. I'm really being brutally honest here and this is beginning slightly to get on my nerves, because I think my learned friend should learn to interpret these orders. It is crystal clear that the order dated the 16th of November is in reference to the order dated the 14th of November. If you look at the order dated the 14th of November you can clearly see that. Fine, all right. I'll try to adopt a slightly mellower tone. I think if we look closely at the 16th of November document, we can see that it contains the assignments issued on the 14th of November because it's crystal clear that the assignments of the 1st Motorised Battalion are one thing, whereas the Assault Detachment 1 assignments remain unchanged in keeping with the decision that was made on the 14th of November. I don't think we are really facing a dilemma here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic, your approach to this issue is open to criticism. You know what you want and you know what you understand these orders to mean. And you are alternately putting your understanding to the witness or submitting it to this Chamber. If there is some matter of evidence about which the witness can speak, you put questions that are non-leading to the witness about it and get his answers. It's then a matter later for your submissions what those orders mean. And you are putting the two processes together at this time. You may not agree with the way an order is being understood or an argument being advanced by the Prosecution about the meaning of an order, but that does not necessarily mean that it is wrong. That's a matter that you have to establish by the end of the day. Just because you have a clear view to the contrary, which may be right, it doesn't mean at this stage that you are in a position simply to assert that from the bar table to us or to the witness and to say no other view is open or possible. So please understand that it is necessary to observe courtesy to views that may differ from yours. They may prove to be wrong. They may prove to be right. Certainly, where this witness can assist with evidence that would help support your view, you may put those questions in your re-examination, the matter, of course, arising out of cross-examination. Now, I'm sorry that became something of a little lecture, but tensions are growing between counsel over this matter, and we feel that it would be important for counsel each to back off a little and understand their role at this stage in the trial is limited and does not involve any argument about their final positions. I hope in the course of that, Mr. Borovic, you're able now to see whether there are any further questions you want to put to this witness about these orders or related matters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I thought we had gone over this with the witness yesterday but since the Prosecutor raised this issue, I felt the need to readdress this issue in my redirect.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So the order of the 14th of November, in accordance with this order, is the 1st Motorised Battalion a part of the 1st Assault Detachment?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO  STIJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In accordance with the order of the 14th of November, the 1st Motorised Battalion is not part of JOD 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: My next question the order defining the tasks, does it stipulate that the 1st Motorised Battalion is part of the Assault Detachment 1?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO  STIJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order of the 14th of November and any further order stipulate that this battalion was never again part of the Assault Detachment 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You were shown an order from the Operations Group South of the 21st of November about the resubordination of the Leva Supoderica Detachment. Now my question to you is: Have you ever seen any order or has anyone from the Prosecution, either in the course of the interview or here in the courtroom, shown you any piece of paper, any order, that would indicate that the Leva Supoderica Detachment was subordinated in any other way than stipulated here?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO  STIJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told the Prosecutor that I had seen this order of the 21st of November for the first time here, and I explained that this was an order about the resubordination of the units within the Operations Group, in which I had no insight.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And did you ever in the area of Milovo Brdo, after the 10th of November, see members of the Territorial Defence detachment, I mean Petrova Gora, and the Leva Supoderica Detachment, did they participate in any activities related to the retention of the lines that had been reached or not?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO  STIJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of the Petrova Gora Detachment and of the Leva Supoderica Detachment passed through this zone as they went on to carry out their task as part of the JOD, but they did not linger in this area at all and they did not have any activities related to the area of Milovo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 19th of November you said that you were in the hospital when my learned colleague asked you about that. The securing of the outer perimeter of the hospital was carried out by any other -- was it carried out by any member of the Petrova Gora Territorial Defence detachment or Leva Supoderica Detachment in addition to Miroslav Radic's company?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO  STIJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was present there in front of the hospital on the 19th of November, apart from some of the soldiers doing their national service and the doctors and nurses who were there in front of the hospital, I did not see any other person.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: At the regular briefing on the 19th and the 20th of November, 1991, did you see the commanders of the Petrova Gora Territorial Defence and Leva Supoderica Detachment or were they absent?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO  STIJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the 10th of November until our return to Belgrade, I did not see the commanders of the Leva Supoderica Detachment and the Petrova Gora Detachment at the briefings in the command of the 1st Motorised Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stijakovic. This concludes my redirect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Borovic. You'll shall pleased to know that that concludes your questioning. The Chamber would like to thank you for your attendance here in The Hague, for the assistance that you've been able to give. You'll be pleased to know that you are now free to go back to your ordinary occupations and interests. Thank you very much. The court officer will show you out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I take up some of this time to make an application? Mr. Mrksic's Defence has filed a motion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can I ask you to pause, Mr. Domazet? Because we have a witness waiting and I had encouraged Ms. Tapuskovic to think that we would go on with the evidence. Two things, the completion of this witness's evidence has taken quite a lot longer than we anticipated; and secondly, I sense that it might not be a bad idea if we gave counsel a slightly earlier break now, before continuing. So that I would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I would suggest that the occasion now has come when we should not think of calling the next witness. We cannot even have the 20 minutes because we take about half of that time to set up the special protection measures, and it's in that context that I apologise to you but I suggest that really the more practical step is to start your witness now first thing tomorrow morning. And Mr. Domazet's motion that he wants to put now perhaps just adds to the realisation that we can't effectively start this witness tonight. Thank you. Yes, Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I more or less expected this outcome. I wanted to present this application while we were waiting for the witness. Mile Mrksic's Defence has filed a motion on the evidence it intends to present and the Prosecution responded on the 6th of October, partially accepting the motion and partly opposing it, and Mile Mrksic's Defence would like to reply to the Prosecution response before the Honourable Chamber rules on this matter. And in fact, the deadline for this reply is tomorrow. Now I would like to ask you for an extension of the deadline by a few days, until Tuesday or Wednesday, in light of the fact that Mr. Vasic left last Saturday and I have been alone, and I hope that his -- the medical procedure he underwent today went well and I hope that he'll be joining us next week. So I really -- this week has really been tough, what with the trial and some other obligations that our team had because we had to complete the stage report until -- by tomorrow. So I really haven't been able to do that, what with the absence of Mr. Vasic, and I would like to respectfully ask you to extend this deadline until mid-next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, by 1.00 p.m. next Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I hope you enjoy the weekend with the submissions. We will adjourn now and resume tomorrow morning at 9.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 13th day of October, 2006, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.41 p.m.,
